This symbol is a placeholder for when one doesn't have a disposition or subfaction that they are part of.
Players who have shields deployed on them through a Medic or Retributionist-Medic.
Players who have been knighted by a Monarch receive this symbol.

Players that have been trapped by a Trapper or Retributionist-Trapper. Trapped players will have their interactors' roles logged and sent to the relevant Trapper. If the trapped target is attacked, the trap will remove all of its logged roles and attack the attacker. The Trapper is notified if the trap attacked someone, and if not, they get a list of roles that interacted with their targets.
Players who have been doused by an Arsonist. Doused players can be ignited by the Arsonist from anywhere.
Targets of a Bounty Hunter will have this symbol on their name. All targets know there is a bounty on their head.
Players who have been doused by a Cryomaniac. Doused players can be frozen by the Cryomaniac from anywhere.
The symbol that means one is part of the Undead subfaction.
Players being tormented by an Executioner. Avoid ejecting them to increase your chances of winning.
Players being watched by a Guardian Angel. Try to recruit them or their GA to your side to increase your chances of winning.
Players being protected by their Guardian Angel.
Players being agonised by a Guesser. If the player is on your team, avoid revealing their role publicly to increase your chances of winning.
The symbol that means one is part of the Cabal subfaction.
The symbol that means one is part of the Reanimated subfaction.
Players that have been infected by a Plaguebearer. Once everyone is infected, the Plaguebearer becomes Pestilence.
This symbol denotes how many stacks of the plague a certain player has.
Survivors who currently have their vests active.
The symbol that means one is part of the Cult subfaction.
Players who are framed by a Framer or Rebel-Framer. Framed players can die without triggering penalties for killers like Vigilante and Assassin.
Players who have been spellbound by a Spellslinger or Rebel-Spellslinger. When all non-Syndicate players are spellbound, the game will immediately end in the Spellslinger's victory.
Players who have been blackmailed by a Blackmailer or Godfather-Blackmailer. Blackmailed players cannot speak in chat.
Players who have been silenced by a Silencer or Rebel-Silencer. Silenced players cannot see anything in chat aside from system messages.

Players who have been blinded by a Grenadier or Godfather-Grenadier. Flashed players cannot see anything as their screen turns white. Exempted players will have their screen dull out slightly to indicate they were flashed.
The player who currently wields the Chaos Drive within the Syndicate faction.
This symbol indicates that they are in the same faction as you, but beware as they could still backstab you.
Players who have been marked by the Ghoul. Marked players will die at the end of the next meeting.
When enabled, the first person to die in the previous game receives a shield of protection in the next game's first round.
Players who are on high alert. Alerted players will attack anyone who interacts with them.
Players being targeted by a Crusader. Crusaded players will attack anyone who interacts with them, or if the Crusader holds the drive, everyone within a certain radius.
Players being targeted by an Ambusher. Ambushed players will attack anyone who interacts with them.

The Cult is a group that can gain massive numbers of followers in one go. It may be weak at the start, but do not underestimate them as their powerful growth as it may overrun you. The Cult is led by the Whisperer.

The Cabal is a greedy organisation. They operate covertly by secretly recruiting people to join their group. The Cabal starts off very strong, making them a high-priority threat. They are led by the Jackal.
The Undead are a group of bloodthirsty vampires who slowly grow their numbers. The longer the game progresses, the higher their elimination priority becomes. They are led by the Dracula.

The Reanimated are individuals who have died yet hold a grudge against the living. This is facilitated by the Necromancer, their leader. Extended periods without confirmed deaths increase suspicion of Necromancer activity.
This mode is nothing special. Everyone is either a basic Crewmate, Impostor, or Anarchist (if alternate intruders is enabled).
This is the main mode of the game. You can customize the chances of roles appearing and set their maximum instances.
This mode has no restrictions on role instances. Each role has a "Uniqueness" property (only 1-2 instances allowed).
A skill-based mode where players race to complete tasks. No killing allowed - victory is determined by task completion speed.
Create custom role sets with exact alignment/faction counts. The "Uniqueness" property applies here, allowing tailored role distributions.
An unofficial Hide & Seek variant with two types: Classic (fixed Hunter numbers) and Infection (Hunters convert others). Only two roles spawn initially.

Each member has a special ability to deduce identities and combat threats. This faction emphasizes teamwork and deduction. As an uninformed majority, Crewmates form most of the player base and lack knowledge of other members. Completing tasks acts as a timer to pressure non-Crew roles.
A destructive faction focused on raw power. Members can kill and use role-specific abilities. As an informed minority, Intruders know each other and coordinate sabotage to disrupt Crew tasks.

A chaotic faction that gains killing power after meetings. Members start with unique abilities and later unlock the "Chaos Drive," enhancing their capabilities. As an informed minority, they coordinate strategically.

A glass cannon faction that starts weak but can become extremely powerful upon completing objectives. Members start with a role specific objective that they must complete to transform into a powerful version of themselves that can greatly affect the flow of a game.

Factionless roles with unique win conditions. Neutrals operate independently in a free-for-all style. As an uninformed minority, they lack team coordination and pursue diverse objectives;some helpful, some not.
A coalition of Neutral Killers and Neophytes. Combines lethal power with conversion abilities, forming a formidable threat. Members coordinate to overwhelm other factions.
An alliance between Intruders and Syndicate. Leverages sabotage, swift kills, and the enhanced "Chaos Drive" to dominate the ship. Focuses on coordinated strikes and resource control.
A joint force of Compliance and Pandorica factions. Boasts a vast arsenal of abilities to overpower the Crew. Represents the ultimate challenge for survival-oriented roles.
Exclusive to special game modes. These roles feature unique mechanics and objectives not found in standard factions. Examples include Hide & Seek variants and task-based competitions.
